text.brief: In late July 1921 thirteen delegates met in a house in the French Concession of Shanghai to found the Chinese Communist Party, with two Comintern agents in the room.
text.record: Hendricus Sneevliet, known as Maring, represented the Communist International at the first congress. The Party joined the Comintern as its Chinese section in 1922 and took its directives ([Resolution of the Second National Congress of the CCP on joining the Third International, July 1922 (text hosted on Wikisource)](https://zh.wikisource.org/zh-hans/%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E5%85%B1%E4%BA%A7%E5%85%9A%E5%8A%A0%E5%85%A5%E7%AC%AC%E4%B8%89%E5%9B%BD%E9%99%85%E5%86%B3%E8%AE%AE%E6%A1%88); [Ukaze on a Rag: Comintern order of 18 July 1922 (International Institute of Social History, Sneevliet Papers)](https://archief.socialhistory.org/en/node/2759)). Chen Duxiu reported to Moscow in June 1922 that the Comintern had supplied almost all of the Party's spending since the previous October ([Twenty-First Century (Chinese University of Hong Kong): article quoting Chen Duxiu's report to the Comintern of June 30, 1922 (secondary)](https://www.cuhk.edu.hk/ics/21c/media/articles/c083-200403013.pdf)).
text.reading: The Party began as a foreign-funded section of a foreign organization, a fact its own histories record. The Party now treats foreign funding of Chinese civil society as a security threat, as its 2017 law on foreign NGOs shows.
text.gapText: Data Architecture. The Republic's government kept no registry of foreign money in its politics.
text.fix: Register foreign funding of political organizations and enforce the registry, the job FARA and Section 117 exist to do.
